cases.title: Given a user-facing creation or change request, when Agent Bridge begins the workflow, then project inspection and CocoSpecs start or resume before implementation planning or mutation.
cases.evidence: Focused guardrail tests prove Agent Bridge performs internal inspection and refuses user-facing mutation planning until the canonical CocoSpec workflow is present and approved.

cases.title: Given an existing CocoSpec, when the workflow resumes, then only the next adaptive question batch is returned and canonical answers are preserved.
cases.evidence: Lifecycle tests prove an existing CocoSpec resumes from canonical state and returns only the next adaptive question batch without overwriting reviewed answers.

cases.title: Given a read-only explanation, audit, or recommendation, when no mutation is requested, then the workflow may stop after inspect and search without requiring lifecycle approval or changing state.
cases.evidence: Agent read-operation tests compare workspace and Git state before and after inspect/search workflows and confirm no mutation.

cases.title: Given visual work, when the CocoSpec is approved, then a visual-reference decision is required before implementation.
cases.evidence: Workflow guardrail tests prove visual work cannot plan a mutation until an explicit reference-or-no-reference decision is bound.

cases.title: Given an image or website reference, when the reference decision is recorded, then CocoRef audits existing components before any missing component is proposed or implemented.
cases.evidence: CocoRef lifecycle tests prove application and framework component inventories are audited before missing reference components are proposed.

cases.title: Given no visual reference, when the user confirms its absence, then a canonical no-reference decision is recorded and the AI may propose a direction using the approved Design Profile and reusable components.
cases.evidence: Workflow tests prove a confirmed no-reference path binds the approved Design Profile hash and reusable component inventory.

cases.title: Given an existing route, API, framework component, or application component that satisfies the requirement, when discovery runs, then it is returned for reuse before a new implementation is proposed.
cases.evidence: Project inspection, documentation search, API lookup, and component-find tests return reusable routes and capabilities with source locations before new implementation.

cases.title: Given an unmet required lifecycle prerequisite, when mutation.plan or mutation.execute is requested, then Agent Bridge refuses it with a stable machine-readable diagnostic and leaves all targets unchanged.
cases.evidence: Mutation guardrail tests assert stable prerequisite diagnostics and unchanged declared files when workflow requirements are absent or stale.

cases.title: Given a new or changed internal link, CTA, route, page, anchor, or API reference, when implementation is planned and verified, then its target exists in the inspected route or document graph.
cases.evidence: Target verification tests resolve changed internal links and routes against the inspected existing-plus-proposed route graph before planning.

cases.title: Given a newly created navigation target, when runtime verification runs, then the target returns a successful or intentional redirect response and does not render a 404, empty destination, or inert action.
cases.evidence: A temporary CocoFrame application is production-built and its newly proposed /dashboard route is fetched successfully with status 200, non-empty Dashboard content, and no 404.

cases.title: Given a link or interactive control, when accessibility verification runs, then it has an accessible name, keyboard behavior, visible focus, and an action matching its label.
cases.evidence: Target declarations and browser E2E checks cover accessible names, keyboard operation, visible focus, and label-to-action integrity.

cases.title: Given an external link that Agent Bridge cannot verify directly, when completion is attempted, then provider-supplied evidence or an explicit unresolved-target diagnostic is required instead of claiming the link works.
cases.evidence: Guardrail tests reject unverifiable external targets with TARGET_NOT_REACHABLE unless sanitized provider evidence is supplied.

cases.title: Given a visual interface, when CocoQA runs, then grid and container alignment, text baselines, icon-label alignment, card and column alignment, spacing rhythm, contrast, overflow, and responsive consistency are measured.
cases.evidence: Product Design Quality tests require alignment, spacing, color, contrast, overflow, and responsive criteria, including the VISUAL_ALIGNMENT_FAILED diagnostic.

cases.title: Given approved viewports and text zoom, when visual alignment is measured, then related elements remain aligned without unintended drift, clipping, overlap, or broken reading order.
cases.evidence: Responsive E2E passed at 320px, phone, tablet, laptop, and 4K profiles plus 200 percent text zoom without unintended overflow or overlap.

cases.title: Given a completed CocoRef, when visual QA runs, then alignment and fidelity are compared against every approved reference criterion and viewport.
cases.evidence: Lifecycle tests prove a completed CocoRef contributes approved reference criteria and a required design-fidelity case to CocoQA.

cases.title: Given no CocoRef, when visual QA runs, then alignment and design-system checks still execute against the approved Design Profile and component rules while fidelity is explicitly not applicable.
cases.evidence: This canonical QA binds cocoframe.design.json and includes alignment/design-system cases while omitting fidelity because no CocoRef applies to this feature.

cases.title: Given missing route evidence, inert links, destructive alignment defects, inaccessible controls, or failed required visual gates, when release approval is attempted, then CocoQA refuses approval.
cases.evidence: QA state-machine and workflow tests prove failed required cases, failed gates, missing targets, inaccessible controls, and destructive alignment defects prevent approval.

cases.title: Given generated routes, clients, OpenAPI, CSS declarations, or API documentation are affected, when implementation completes, then only the owning generators refresh those artifacts and verification checks their freshness.
cases.evidence: npm run generate, API documentation generation, npm run check, and generated-artifact assertions passed; generated files were refreshed only through owning commands.

cases.title: Given two supported AI providers, when they perform the workflow, then the same provider-independent contracts, prerequisite checks, diagnostics, and result structures are used.
cases.evidence: In-process and MCP adapter tests use the same versioned descriptors, prerequisite diagnostics, workflow hashes, and structurally equivalent result contracts.

cases.title: Given a completed workflow, when the AI reports completion, then it lists lifecycle states, reference decisions, reused components, approved mutations, verified links and targets, visual-alignment evidence, quality gates, defects, and unresolved risks.
cases.evidence: Operation results and generated QA reports include lifecycle/reference state, workflow hashes, affected targets, approvals, verified targets, gate evidence, defects, and unresolved risks.

cases.title: Existing framework and application components are audited before a new component is proposed.
cases.evidence: Component discovery and CocoRef audit tests prove @cocoframe/ui and application inventories are searched before a missing component is proposed.

cases.title: Project appearance is derived from the approved semantic design profile instead of duplicated hardcoded styles.
cases.evidence: The canonical Design Profile is hash-bound to the workflow, and Product Design Quality tests require semantic tokens instead of duplicated hardcoded styles.

cases.title: Grid and container edges, text baselines, icon-label pairs, cards, and columns remain consistently aligned at every approved viewport and zoom level.
cases.evidence: Alignment is a mandatory design principle covering containers, baselines, icon-label pairs, cards, and columns; responsive E2E passed all approved viewports and zoom.

cases.title: Spacing values follow the approved scale and produce a consistent layout rhythm.
cases.evidence: Design criteria and profile validation require the approved spacing scale; Product Design Quality focused tests passed.

cases.title: Semantic color usage remains consistent across equivalent states and components.
cases.evidence: Design criteria and profile validation require consistent semantic color roles; Product Design Quality focused tests passed.

cases.title: Text, focus indicators, controls, and meaningful graphics satisfy the approved WCAG 2.2 AA contrast thresholds.
cases.evidence: WCAG 2.2 AA contrast is required by the canonical QA decisions; browser checks including forced-colors passed.

cases.title: Typography uses the approved family, scale, weight, line height, and readable wrapping.
cases.evidence: Design profile tests validate the approved typography family, scale, weight, line height, and wrapping rules.

cases.title: Corners use the approved radius scale consistently.
cases.evidence: Design profile tests validate consistent use of the approved semantic radius scale.

cases.title: Shadows and elevation communicate hierarchy consistently without obscuring focus or contrast.
cases.evidence: Design profile tests validate semantic elevation while preserving focus visibility and contrast.

cases.title: Icons use the approved catalog, family, sizes, alignment, and accessible labeling.
cases.evidence: Design criteria require approved icon catalog reuse, sizing, alignment, and accessible labels; catalog E2E passed.

cases.title: Approved viewports and text zoom have no unintended horizontal overflow, clipping, or overlapping controls.
cases.evidence: Responsive browser checks passed from 320px through 4K and at 200 percent text zoom without unintended horizontal overflow, clipping, or overlap.

cases.title: The interface reflows from 320 pixels through 4K at every approved viewport.
cases.evidence: Critical-page responsive E2E passed the approved 320px, phone, tablet, laptop, and 4K viewport profiles.

cases.title: Keyboard, focus, semantic, announcement, forced-colors, and reduced-motion behavior satisfy the approved target.
cases.evidence: Keyboard, focus, semantics, announcements, forced-colors, and reduced-motion requirements are represented in QA; accessibility-focused E2E passed.

cases.title: Useful server-rendered output exists without browser JavaScript.
cases.evidence: Build and runtime tests confirm useful server-rendered output exists before browser JavaScript hydration.

cases.title: Keyboard, focus, labels, errors, and semantic structure satisfy the approved accessibility target.
cases.evidence: Accessibility tests and browser E2E passed keyboard, focus, labels, errors, and semantic structure checks.

cases.title: Every changed internal link, CTA, route, anchor, and API target returns successful content or an intentional redirect; external targets have sanitized provider evidence.
cases.evidence: Target verifier tests cover existing and proposed routes, anchors, external evidence, and a real production fetch of /dashboard returning successful content.

cases.title: Every changed link and control has an accessible name, keyboard behavior, visible focus, and an action matching its label.
cases.evidence: Changed controls are statically declared with accessibility expectations and verified by keyboard/focus browser tests; inert or mismatched actions are rejected.

cases.title: The feature remains usable across the approved viewport and device range without horizontal overflow.
cases.evidence: Responsive E2E passed all approved viewport profiles without unintended horizontal overflow.
